content.page_title: Immediate/early discharge and chronic treatment & prevention of recurrence (PE guideline)
content.immediate_early_discharge_summary: Decision on immediate or early discharge of patients with acute pulmonary embolism (PE) should consider exclusion of intermediate-risk PE on clinical grounds alone vs assessment of right ventricular (RV) dysfunction or myocardial injury by imaging or laboratory biomarkers. Combining clinical scores (e.g. PESI or sPESI) with imaging findings or biomarker levels increases prognostic sensitivity. It is recommended to exclude RV dysfunction and right heart thrombi if immediate or early (within the first 24–48 h) discharge is planned.

key_trial_findings_on_early_discharge.selection: patients selected by clinical criteria and absence of RV dysfunction
key_trial_findings_on_early_discharge.inclusion_rate_approximate: ≈20% of screened unselected patients with PE were included

interim_analysis.PE_related_deaths: none reported in the trial interim analysis

key_trial_findings_on_early_discharge.conclusion: Given existing evidence and catastrophic risk if a patient with acute PE is falsely judged low risk, plus ease of assessing RV size/function, it is wise to exclude RV dysfunction before early discharge.

section_8_chronic_treatment_and_preventi.aim: Complete treatment of the acute PE episode and prevent long-term recurrence of venous thromboembolism (VTE).
section_8_chronic_treatment_and_preventi.initial_phase_reference: Current drugs and regimens for the initial phase and first months described in section 6 (referenced).

evidence_from_randomized_studies.patient_population: Most randomized studies on long-term anticoagulation for VTE included patients with deep vein thrombosis (DVT), with or without PE; only two randomized studies specifically focused on patients with PE.
evidence_from_randomized_studies.recurrence_incidence: Incidence of recurrent VTE does not appear to depend on whether the first event presented as PE or proximal DVT.
evidence_from_randomized_studies.pattern_of_recurrence: In patients who had a PE, recurrent VTE more frequently recurs as PE; in patients who had a DVT, recurrences tend to be more often DVT.
evidence_from_randomized_studies.case_fatality_consequence: Case fatality rate of recurrent VTE in patients who previously had a PE is about twice as high as that of VTE recurrence after DVT.

practical_recommendations_and_considerat: Use PESI or sPESI for clinical triage but combine with assessment of feasibility of early discharge and home treatment.
If PESI- or sPESI-based approach chosen, combine with imaging or biomarker assessment when determining safety for early discharge.
Assess RV size and function at presentation by echocardiography or evaluate CT pulmonary angiography (CTPA) for RV dysfunction/right heart thrombi prior to early discharge.
content.references_notes: Multiple references cited in the original text supporting sensitivity improvements when combining clinical criteria with imaging/biomarkers and details of the multicentre trial (specific citation numbers present in source). Some original text included encoding artifacts (e.g., character encoding for some symbols).
